whyItMatters: The 45-Degree Leg Press builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
executionSteps: Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
coachingTips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Caved knees are a weaker position and rob power from the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and turns the squat into a good morning.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

breathingGuidance: Take a big breath at the top, hold it through the descent and drive, then exhale at the top.
tempoGuidance: Lower under control for about two counts, then stand with intent.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Aim for thighs at or below parallel while keeping your heels flat on the floor. Take the quadriceps through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.
beginnerNotes: Start with a box or bench behind you to learn consistent depth.
equipmentSetup: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
difficultyConsiderations: The 45-Degree Leg Press is a compound machine movement. Because the machine guides the path, put your attention on driving with the target muscle. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because the machine guides the path, so there is little balance to manage, and it coordinates several joints at once.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Cable Bulgarian Split Squat once you can control this one for all your reps.

setupInstructions: Ease into the starting position without forcing the range.
Set a comfortable position you can control before moving.
executionSteps: Move to the first point of tension, not into pain.
Ease slightly deeper on each exhale.
Hold the end position briefly, then return smoothly to the start.
coachingTips: Move to the first point of tension rather than into pain.
Breathe out as you ease a little deeper into the range.
Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.

Holding your breath while you hold the position.
Snapping quickly from one rep to the next.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Forcing or bouncing into an end range.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Forcing past your range fights the stretch instead of easing it and does little for mobility.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly to gentle tension and let it ease with your breath.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Holding your breath while you hold the position.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Holding your breath tenses you up and stops you easing deeper into the range.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep breathing slowly and let each exhale ease you a little deeper.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Snapping quickly from one rep to the next.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Snapping through reps skips the controlled range that mobility work depends on.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly into and out of each repetition.

tempoGuidance: Move slowly and hold positions rather than bouncing.

cueHierarchy: Move to the first point of tension rather than into pain.

Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.

setupInstructions: Set your position and take the slack out of your midsection before you begin.
Start each rep from a controlled, stable position.
executionSteps: Move slowly and deliberately through the working range.
Pause briefly where your midsection is working hardest.
Control the return rather than dropping quickly at the end.
coachingTips: Move under control — no yanking or rushing the reps.
Curl your ribs toward your hips rather than pulling with your neck.
Keep the tension on your midsection, not your hip flexors or lower back.
Curl your ribs toward your hips and feel your abs shorten.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
Rushing through reps with momentum.
Arching the lower back away from a braced position.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Pulling your head does the work your abs should, so your midsection gets less out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hands light and lead the movement from your midsection.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing through reps with momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Momentum does the work your abs should, so the set does less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow each rep down and control both directions.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back away from a braced position.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A loose lower back leaks force and takes the work off your abs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your ribs down and your midsection tight through the whole rep.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you contract, breathe in as you return.
tempoGuidance: Move slowly in both directions and avoid using momentum.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Work through a range you can control without your lower back taking over. Take the rectus abdominis through its full working range each rep.

whyItMatters: The Adductor Rock-Back builds strength and size in your adductors. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Set your working hip in position with your torso stable.
Start from a controlled position without momentum.
executionSteps: Move the working leg through its range while keeping your torso still.
Squeeze the working glute at the end of each rep.
Lower the leg under control back to the start without resting.
coachingTips: Squeeze the working glute at the top of each rep for a beat.
Keep your torso still and move only at the hip.
Control the return rather than letting the leg drop.
Squeeze your inner thighs together through the working range.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to swing the leg higher.
Rushing reps and losing the glute contraction.
Arching the lower back to gain more range.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Twisting the torso to swing the leg higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Twisting fakes extra range and takes the work off the working hip.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hips and torso square and move only at the working hip.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing reps and losing the glute contraction.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Without a squeeze at the top your glutes do far less of the work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow down and pause to feel the working glute at the top.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back to gain more range.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: The extra range comes from your spine, not the target muscle, so it adds little.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your lower back flat and move only as far as the hip allows.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you contract, breathe in as you return.
tempoGuidance: Move with control and pause at peak contraction.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Work through the range where you feel the glute working, without your back compensating. Take the adductors through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Squeeze the working glute at the top of each rep for a beat.
Squeeze your inner thighs together through the working range.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Keep your torso still and move only at the hip.
Control the return rather than letting the leg drop.

beginnerNotes: Use no load or a light band until you feel the glute working.

Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

whyItMatters: The Air Bike builds your aerobic base, work capacity and conditioning.
setupInstructions: Set the machine to your working effort and settle into a rhythm before pushing.
Set your effort to a pace you can sustain for the planned duration.
Settle into a rhythm before pushing the pace.
executionSteps: Hold a steady, repeatable rhythm for the working duration.
Keep your breathing matched to your pace throughout.
Adjust your effort so the last minute feels as controlled as the first.
coachingTips: Settle into a cadence you can hold for the full effort.
Breathe rhythmically and in time with your pace.
Build the pace gradually rather than starting too hard.
Keep a smooth, round pedal stroke and a steady cadence.
commonMistakes: Starting too fast and fading in the second half.
Tensing the shoulders and upper body while working.
Letting the effort drift down whenever your attention wanders.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Starting too fast and fading in the second half.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A fast start you cannot hold means the back half of the effort suffers.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Open at a pace you could hold to the end, then build.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Tensing the shoulders and upper body while working.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Tension up top wastes energy that should go into your legs and lungs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Relax your hands, shoulders and face so the effort stays in your legs and lungs.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the effort drift down whenever your attention wanders.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Coasting drops the training effect for that stretch of the effort.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Check your pace regularly and hold it steady to the end.

tempoGuidance: Hold a sustainable, repeatable pace for the target duration.
cueHierarchy: Settle into a cadence you can hold for the full effort.
Keep a smooth, round pedal stroke and a steady cadence.
Breathe rhythmically and in time with your pace.
Build the pace gradually rather than starting too hard.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add pace changes or intervals to raise the training stimulus.

whyItMatters: The Alternating Curl builds strength and size in your biceps. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Choose a pair you can control for every planned rep and get them into position cleanly.
Set a tall torso with your upper arms pinned against your sides.
Start with your arms straight and the load under control.
executionSteps: Bend your elbows and curl the load up while keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top for a beat.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
coachingTips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Turn your pinky slightly up at the top to finish the squeeze.
Lower all the way until your arm is straight each rep.
Keep the tension on your biceps and stop your elbows from drifting forward.
Control each dumbbell independently so your stronger side doesn’t take over.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
Cutting the lower-half of the range short.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A torso swing starts the curl with momentum instead of your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stand tall and keep your upper arms fixed against your sides.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Moving the elbows turns a curl into a partial front raise and takes tension off your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your elbows under your shoulders and stop the curl where your upper arm wants to move.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the lower-half of the range short.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the bottom half leaves strength and size on the table.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Straighten your arm fully at the bottom of each rep.

difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

setupInstructions: Set the pulley to the right height, attach the handle, and step back to remove the slack before your first rep.
Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
executionSteps: Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
coachingTips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Keep steady tension on the cable through the whole range, including the return.

Cutting the depth short above parallel.
Letting the cable yank your arm back at the end of the rep.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Giving in to the cable skips the lowering phase, cutting the work in half.

Set your shoulders back and down before you start walking.

Set the load down under control at the end of the distance rather than dropping it.

Lower your hips under control back toward the floor.

Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
executionSteps: Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
coachingTips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.

Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Caved knees are a weaker position and rob power from the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

setupInstructions: Set your hands about shoulder-width, slightly wider than your chest.

Tuck your ribs down and brace before the first rep.

Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a beat.
Lower your hips under control back toward the floor.
coachingTips: Drive through your heels, not your toes.
Finish each rep by squeezing your glutes at the top, not by arching your lower back.
Keep your ribs down and your chin slightly tucked so the work stays in your glutes.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.

Pushing through the toes so the heels lift.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Extra height from your spine, not your hips, means your glutes do less of the work.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes your glutes do less and the hip drive weakens.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot down and drive through your heels.

Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.

Let your knees track in line with your toes.

Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.

whyItMatters: The Lateral Hurdle Hop builds strength and size in your glutes, adductors, erector spinae and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
Set your feet about hip-width with the load close to your shins.
Set your back flat and take a breath into your belly before you pull.
executionSteps: Push your hips back and let your knees bend slightly as the load lowers.
Keep the load brushing your legs the whole way.
Stand up by driving your hips forward until you are tall.
coachingTips: Push your hips back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Keep the load in contact with your legs from start to finish.
Finish by squeezing your glutes, not by leaning back past standing.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as the load leaves the floor.
Turning the hinge into a squat by bending the knees too early.
Hyperextending and leaning back at the top.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rounding the lower back as the load leaves the floor.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A rounded back is the weakest position to lift from.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Set your back flat and lift your chest before the load moves.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Turning the hinge into a squat by bending the knees too early.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Early knee bend takes the stretch and work off your hamstrings and glutes.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Send your hips backward first and let the knees follow.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Hyperextending and leaning back at the top.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Leaning back past standing loads your lower back and adds nothing to the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop when you are standing tall with your glutes squeezed.

breathingGuidance: Breathe in at the top, brace, hold through the lift, then exhale once you are standing.
tempoGuidance: Lower for about two to three counts, then drive up with intent.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch with a flat back — depth is limited by your hamstrings, not the floor. Take the glutes through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Push your hips back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
Keep the load in contact with your legs from start to finish.
Finish by squeezing your glutes, not by leaning back past standing.
advancedCoachingNotes: Pause just below the knee to build control in the stretched position.
beginnerNotes: Practice the hip hinge with a light load or dowel to groove the pattern first.
equipmentSetup: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
difficultyConsiderations: The Lateral Hurdle Hop is a compound plyometric movement. The box fixes the height, so land and stand on it under full control. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you can scale the effort and load to your level, and it coordinates several joints at once.

whyItMatters: The Lateral Lunge builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Set a tall chest and brace before you descend.
executionSteps: Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
coachingTips: Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your foot.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up as you descend and stand.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward.
Letting the heels lift off the floor.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Knees caving in is a weaker position and takes force off your glutes.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the heels lift off the floor.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes you lose your base and shift the squat onto your knees.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot planted and your weight over the mid-foot.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

breathingGuidance: Breathe in on the way down, exhale as you stand.
tempoGuidance: Lower under control for about two counts, then stand with intent.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Lower to at least thighs-parallel and stand up tall each rep. Take the quadriceps through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up as you descend and stand.
advancedCoachingNotes: Slow the descent or add a pause at the bottom to increase the challenge.
beginnerNotes: Lower to a box or bench behind you to learn consistent depth.
difficultyConsiderations: The Lateral Lunge is a compound bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it coordinates several joints at once.

whyItMatters: The Leaning Lateral Raise builds strength and size in your lateral deltoids. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Choose a pair you can control for every planned rep and get them into position cleanly.
Set a tall torso with a slight bend in your elbows.
Start with the load under control at your sides or front.
executionSteps: Lead with your elbows and raise the load to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the load under control to the start.
coachingTips: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower under control rather than dropping the load.
Lead with your elbow and feel the side of your shoulder do the work.
Control each dumbbell independently so your stronger side doesn’t take over.
commonMistakes: Swinging the load up with the torso.
Raising the load well above shoulder height and shrugging.
Letting the wrists roll or drop under the load.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging the load up with the torso.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Body swing does the lifting, so your shoulders get little out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your torso still and raise the load with your shoulders, not momentum.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Raising the load well above shoulder height and shrugging.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Going too high brings your traps in and takes the work off the muscle you want.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop at shoulder height and keep your traps relaxed.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the wrists roll or drop under the load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Bent wrists leak force and move the effort away from the muscle you want.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your wrists flat and level with your forearms throughout.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
tempoGuidance: Raise with control and lower for about two counts.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Raise to shoulder height and lower to a light stretch at the start. Take the lateral deltoids through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height.
Lead with your elbow and feel the side of your shoulder do the work.
Control each dumbbell independently so your stronger side doesn’t take over.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower under control rather than dropping the load.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a pause at shoulder height before lowering.
beginnerNotes: Use a light load and stop the moment your form breaks down.
equipmentSetup: Choose a pair you can control for every planned rep and get them into position cleanly.
difficultyConsiderations: The Leaning Lateral Raise is an isolation dumbbell movement. Each dumbbell is balanced on its own, so both sides have to pull their own weight. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

progressionGuidance.regressionReason: Drop back to Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise to groove the movement before you add load or complexity.

whyItMatters: The Leg Extension builds strength and size in your quadriceps. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set the pad against the front of your lower shins and line your knees up with the pivot.
Start with your knees bent and the resistance under control.
executionSteps: Straighten your knees to lift the resistance until your legs are nearly straight.
Squeeze your quads hard at the top for a beat.
Lower under control until your knees are bent back to the start.
coachingTips: Straighten your knees fully and squeeze your quads at the top.
Move only at the knees — keep your hips and back against the seat.
Lower under control rather than letting the weight drop.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Swinging or using momentum to fling the weight up.
Cutting the top short of a full knee extension.
Letting the weight slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging or using momentum to fling the weight up.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A swung weight is lifted by momentum, not your quads.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move at a controlled speed and let your quads do the work.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the top short of a full knee extension.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Stopping short of lockout leaves the peak quad contraction untrained.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Straighten your knees fully and hold the squeeze for a beat.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Dropping the weight skips the lowering phase, where a lot of the muscle work happens.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower under control until your knees are bent back to the start.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you straighten your knees, breathe in as you lower.
tempoGuidance: Extend with control and lower for about two counts.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Move from bent knees to a full, straight-knee squeeze. Take the quadriceps through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Straighten your knees fully and squeeze your quads at the top.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
Move only at the knees — keep your hips and back against the seat.
Lower under control rather than letting the weight drop.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a pause at full extension for a stronger quad contraction.
beginnerNotes: Use a light weight you can control through the full range.
equipmentSetup: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
difficultyConsiderations: The Leg Extension is an isolation machine movement. Because the machine guides the path, put your attention on driving with the target muscle. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because the machine guides the path, so there is little balance to manage, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Single-Leg Leg Extension once you can control this one for all your reps.

whyItMatters: The Light Sled Sprint builds your aerobic base, work capacity and conditioning.
setupInstructions: Load the sled to a weight you can move steadily and check the surface is clear ahead.
Set your effort to a pace you can sustain for the planned duration.
Settle into a rhythm before pushing the pace.
executionSteps: Hold a steady, repeatable rhythm for the working duration.
Keep your breathing matched to your pace throughout.
Adjust your effort so the last minute feels as controlled as the first.
coachingTips: Settle into a cadence you can hold for the full effort.
Breathe rhythmically and in time with your pace.
Build the pace gradually rather than starting too hard.
Run tall with a quick, light cadence and relaxed shoulders and hands.
commonMistakes: Starting too fast and fading in the second half.
Tensing the shoulders and upper body while working.
Letting the effort drift down whenever your attention wanders.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Starting too fast and fading in the second half.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A fast start you cannot hold means the back half of the effort suffers.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Open at a pace you could hold to the end, then build.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Tensing the shoulders and upper body while working.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Tension up top wastes energy that should go into your legs and lungs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Relax your hands, shoulders and face so the effort stays in your legs and lungs.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the effort drift down whenever your attention wanders.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Coasting drops the training effect for that stretch of the effort.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Check your pace regularly and hold it steady to the end.

tempoGuidance: Hold a sustainable, repeatable pace for the target duration.
cueHierarchy: Settle into a cadence you can hold for the full effort.
Run tall with a quick, light cadence and relaxed shoulders and hands.
Breathe rhythmically and in time with your pace.
Build the pace gradually rather than starting too hard.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add pace changes or intervals to raise the training stimulus.
beginnerNotes: Use intervals of easier effort to build duration over time.
equipmentSetup: Load the sled to a weight you can move steadily and check the surface is clear ahead.
difficultyConsiderations: The Light Sled Sprint is a sled movement. The sled only loads you while you drive it, so keep a steady, forceful pace. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you can scale the pace and duration to your fitness.

whyItMatters: The Low Row builds strength and size in your upper back, biceps, latissimus dorsi and rear deltoids. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set the pulley to the right height, attach the handle, and step back to remove the slack before your first rep.
Set your torso and let your working arm hang with the shoulder blade relaxed forward.
Set a stable base before you begin pulling.
executionSteps: Pull your elbow back toward your hip, leading with the elbow.
Draw the load to your lower ribs and squeeze your shoulder blade back.
Lower under control until your arm is straight and the shoulder blade reaches forward.
coachingTips: Lead with your elbow, not your hand.
Draw the load toward your belt line rather than your chest.
Let your shoulder blade slide back and down at the top of each rep.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Keep steady tension on the cable through the whole range, including the return.
commonMistakes: Yanking with the lower back and using momentum.
Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear while pulling.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
Letting the cable yank your arm back at the end of the rep.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Yanking with the lower back and using momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Yanking uses your back and momentum instead of the muscles you are rowing with.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your torso still and let your arm and shoulder blade do the work.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear while pulling.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shrugging shoulder takes the pull off your back and into your traps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your shoulder down and pull your elbow straight back.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the stretch removes the part of the range that builds the most.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Let your arm fully straighten and your shoulder blade reach forward before the next rep.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the cable yank your arm back at the end of the rep.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Giving in to the cable skips the lowering phase, cutting the work in half.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return against the cable tension rather than giving in to it.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you pull, breathe in as you return under control.
tempoGuidance: Pull with intent, then lower for about two counts.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Reach into a full stretch at the bottom and pull until your shoulder blade is fully retracted. Take the upper back through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Lead with your elbow, not your hand.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Keep steady tension on the cable through the whole range, including the return.
Draw the load toward your belt line rather than your chest.
Let your shoulder blade slide back and down at the top of each rep.
advancedCoachingNotes: Pause and squeeze for one count at the fully retracted position.
beginnerNotes: Use a load you can pull without leaning back or jerking.
equipmentSetup: Set the pulley to the right height, attach the handle, and step back to remove the slack before your first rep.
difficultyConsiderations: The Low Row is a compound cable movement. The cable holds constant tension on the muscle through the whole range, including the return. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because the cable is stable and easy to control, and it coordinates several joints at once.

progressionGuidance.regressionReason: Drop back to Machine Low Row to groove the movement before you add load or complexity.

whyItMatters: The Low-to-High Fly builds strength and size in your chest, front deltoids and triceps. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set the pulley to the right height, attach the handle, and step back to remove the slack before your first rep.
Set your grip evenly and pull your shoulder blades down and together.
Set your feet and create full-body tension before you begin.
executionSteps: Lower the load under control toward the middle of your chest.
Keep your forearms vertical as you lower.
Press back to a full lockout.
coachingTips: Keep the load stacked directly over your elbows.
Tuck your elbows to about 45 degrees from your torso.
Drive your shoulder blades back and down and hold that position.
Think about squeezing your chest to drive the movement, not just pushing with your arms.
Keep steady tension on the cable through the whole range, including the return.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Bouncing the load off the chest.
Losing the shoulder-blade set at the bottom.
Letting the cable yank your arm back at the end of the rep.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.

Set your torso and let your working arm hang with the shoulder blade relaxed forward.
Set a stable base before you begin pulling.
executionSteps: Pull your elbow back toward your hip, leading with the elbow.
Draw the load to your lower ribs and squeeze your shoulder blade back.
Lower under control until your arm is straight and the shoulder blade reaches forward.
coachingTips: Lead with your elbow, not your hand.
Draw the load toward your belt line rather than your chest.
Let your shoulder blade slide back and down at the top of each rep.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Move the ball with intent and catch or reset it under control each rep.
commonMistakes: Yanking with the lower back and using momentum.
Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear while pulling.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Yanking with the lower back and using momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Yanking uses your back and momentum instead of the muscles you are rowing with.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your torso still and let your arm and shoulder blade do the work.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear while pulling.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shrugging shoulder takes the pull off your back and into your traps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your shoulder down and pull your elbow straight back.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the stretch removes the part of the range that builds the most.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Let your arm fully straighten and your shoulder blade reach forward before the next rep.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you pull, breathe in as you return under control.
tempoGuidance: Pull with intent, then lower for about two counts.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Reach into a full stretch at the bottom and pull until your shoulder blade is fully retracted. Take the upper back through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Lead with your elbow, not your hand.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Move the ball with intent and catch or reset it under control each rep.
Draw the load toward your belt line rather than your chest.
Let your shoulder blade slide back and down at the top of each rep.
advancedCoachingNotes: Pause and squeeze for one count at the fully retracted position.
beginnerNotes: Use a load you can pull without leaning back or jerking.
equipmentSetup: Pick a ball weight you can control and clear the space around you before you start.
difficultyConsiderations: The Medicine Ball Shot-Put Throw is a compound medicine-ball movement. The ball lets you accelerate and release or catch it, so move it explosively. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you can scale the effort and load to your level, and it coordinates several joints at once.

whyItMatters: The Medicine Ball Squat to Throw builds strength and size in your upper back, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Pick a ball weight you can control and clear the space around you before you start.
Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
executionSteps: Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
coachingTips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Move the ball with intent and catch or reset it under control each rep.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Caved knees are a weaker position and rob power from the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and turns the squat into a good morning.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

breathingGuidance: Take a big breath at the top, hold it through the descent and drive, then exhale at the top.
tempoGuidance: Lower under control for about two counts, then stand with intent.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Aim for thighs at or below parallel while keeping your heels flat on the floor. Take the upper back through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Pull with your back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, not just your arms.
Move the ball with intent and catch or reset it under control each rep.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.
beginnerNotes: Start with a box or bench behind you to learn consistent depth.
equipmentSetup: Pick a ball weight you can control and clear the space around you before you start.

difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you can scale the effort and load to your level, and it coordinates several joints at once.

Set your position and take the slack out of your midsection before you begin.
Start each rep from a controlled, stable position.

Pause briefly where your midsection is working hardest.
Control the return rather than dropping quickly at the end.

Curl your ribs toward your hips and feel your abs shorten.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Pulling your head does the work your abs should, so your midsection gets less out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hands light and lead the movement from your midsection.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing through reps with momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Momentum does the work your abs should, so the set does less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow each rep down and control both directions.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back away from a braced position.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A loose lower back leaks force and takes the work off your abs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your ribs down and your midsection tight through the whole rep.

whyItMatters: The Multi-Hip Abduction builds strength and size in your abductors. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set your working hip in position with your torso stable.
Start from a controlled position without momentum.
executionSteps: Move the working leg through its range while keeping your torso still.
Squeeze the working glute at the end of each rep.
Lower the leg under control back to the start without resting.
coachingTips: Squeeze the working glute at the top of each rep for a beat.
Keep your torso still and move only at the hip.
Control the return rather than letting the leg drop.
Drive your leg outward and feel the side of your hip work.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to swing the leg higher.
Rushing reps and losing the glute contraction.
Arching the lower back to gain more range.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Twisting the torso to swing the leg higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Twisting fakes extra range and takes the work off the working hip.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hips and torso square and move only at the working hip.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing reps and losing the glute contraction.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Without a squeeze at the top your glutes do far less of the work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow down and pause to feel the working glute at the top.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back to gain more range.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: The extra range comes from your spine, not the target muscle, so it adds little.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your lower back flat and move only as far as the hip allows.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

whyItMatters: The Reverse Hack Squat builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.

Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.

Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.

setupInstructions: Load the sled to a weight you can move steadily and check the surface is clear ahead.
Set a stable starting position appropriate to the movement.
Take up any slack and set your position before the first rep.
executionSteps: Move through the intended range under control from start to finish.
Keep the working muscles under tension rather than using momentum.
Return to the start under control before the next repetition.
coachingTips: Move under control through the full range of the movement.
Keep your torso stable unless the movement itself requires it to move.
Match your effort and range on both sides if the movement works one side at a time.

Using a swing or momentum to get through the hardest point.
Shortening the range to complete more repetitions.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing the movement and losing control of the load or your body.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rushing hands the work to momentum instead of your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow each repetition down and control both directions.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Move deliberately and let the working muscles do the work.

whyItMatters: The Scapular Push-Up builds strength and size in your chest, front deltoids and triceps. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set your hands about shoulder-width, slightly wider than your chest.
Set a straight line from your head to your heels and brace before you begin.
executionSteps: Lower your chest under control toward the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked to about 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
coachingTips: Keep a straight line from your head to your heels throughout.
Tuck your elbows to about 45 degrees rather than flaring them wide.
Lower until your chest is just off the floor for a full range.
Think about squeezing your chest to drive the movement, not just pushing with your arms.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Only lowering partway before pressing back up.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Sagging hips break the plank line and shift load to your lower back.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Squeeze your glutes and keep a straight line from head to heels.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Flared elbows put your shoulders in a weaker, less comfortable pressing position.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Point your elbows back toward your hips as you lower.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Only lowering partway before pressing back up.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Half reps train a fraction of the range and build less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your chest is just off the floor each rep.

breathingGuidance: Breathe in as you lower, exhale as you press up.
tempoGuidance: Lower for about two counts, then press up with intent.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Lower until your chest is just off the floor and press to straight arms. Take the chest through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Keep a straight line from your head to your heels throughout.
Think about squeezing your chest to drive the movement, not just pushing with your arms.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Tuck your elbows to about 45 degrees rather than flaring them wide.
Lower until your chest is just off the floor for a full range.
advancedCoachingNotes: Elevate your feet or pause at the bottom to make it harder.
beginnerNotes: Do the movement from your knees or with your hands on a raised surface until you can complete full reps.
difficultyConsiderations: The Scapular Push-Up is a compound bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it coordinates several joints at once.

whyItMatters: The Scapular Wall Slide builds strength and size in your rear deltoids. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Set a tall torso with a slight bend in your elbows.
Start with the load under control at your sides or front.
executionSteps: Lead with your elbows and raise the load to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the load under control to the start.
coachingTips: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower under control rather than dropping the load.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders and pull your elbows back and apart.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Swinging the load up with the torso.
Raising the load well above shoulder height and shrugging.
Letting the wrists roll or drop under the load.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging the load up with the torso.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Body swing does the lifting, so your shoulders get little out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your torso still and raise the load with your shoulders, not momentum.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Raising the load well above shoulder height and shrugging.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Going too high brings your traps in and takes the work off the muscle you want.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop at shoulder height and keep your traps relaxed.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the wrists roll or drop under the load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Bent wrists leak force and move the effort away from the muscle you want.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your wrists flat and level with your forearms throughout.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
tempoGuidance: Raise with control and lower for about two counts.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Raise to shoulder height and lower to a light stretch at the start. Take the rear deltoids through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders and pull your elbows back and apart.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower under control rather than dropping the load.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a pause at shoulder height before lowering.
beginnerNotes: Use a light load and stop the moment your form breaks down.
difficultyConsiderations: The Scapular Wall Slide is an isolation bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

whyItMatters: The Box Jump builds strength and size in your glutes, quadriceps and calves. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
Set a stable, athletic base with your feet under your hips.
Load your hips and take a breath before the explosive rep.
executionSteps: Be explosive on the way up, moving the load or your body as fast as possible.
Absorb the landing or return softly through your hips and knees.
Reset to a stable, balanced position before the next rep.
coachingTips: Be explosive on the way up and controlled on the way down.
Land softly on your mid-foot, absorbing through your hips and knees.
Reset fully between reps rather than rushing the next one.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged with a hard, loud impact.
Rushing reps and losing power output.
Letting the knees collapse inward on landing.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Landing stiff-legged with a hard, loud impact.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A stiff landing wastes the force your legs should be absorbing.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Land quietly and let your hips and knees bend to absorb the force.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing reps and losing power output.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rushed reps are less explosive, and power is the whole point of the movement.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Take a full reset between reps so each one is maximally explosive.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees collapse inward on landing.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A collapsed-knee landing is a weak position to absorb force.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Land with your knees tracking over your toes and your hips back.

breathingGuidance: Take a breath and brace before each rep, then exhale on the effort.
tempoGuidance: Explode on the effort; land and reset under full control.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Complete the full jump, throw or drive, then reset before the next rep. Take the glutes and quadriceps through their full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Be explosive on the way up and controlled on the way down.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Land softly on your mid-foot, absorbing through your hips and knees.
Reset fully between reps rather than rushing the next one.
advancedCoachingNotes: Increase height, distance or load only while landings stay quiet and controlled.
beginnerNotes: Start with lower height or lighter load and step down between reps.
equipmentSetup: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
safetyNotes: When you fatigue, step down rather than jumping down between reps.
difficultyConsiderations: The Box Jump is a plyometric movement. The box fixes the height, so land and stand on it under full control. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because you can scale the effort and load to your level.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Box Jump once you can control this one for all your reps.

whyItMatters: The Calf Raise builds strength and size in your calves. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set the balls of your feet on a stable surface with your heels free to drop.
Find a light hold for balance if you need it.
executionSteps: Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a beat at the top.
Lower under control until you feel a full stretch through your calves.
coachingTips: Rise as high onto your toes as possible at the top.
Lower under control into a full stretch at the bottom.
Pause briefly at the top to remove any bounce.
Rise all the way onto your toes and squeeze your calves at the top.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Short bounces use the tendon’s spring instead of your calves, so they do less work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Pause at the top and control a full stretch at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the stretch removes the part of the range that builds the most.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Let your heels drop below the platform for a full stretch.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rolling out sends force through the outside of your foot instead of your calves.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Drive evenly through your big toe and keep your ankles stacked.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

breathingGuidance: Exhale as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
tempoGuidance: Rise with control, pause at the top, then lower slowly.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Move from a deep heel-dropped stretch to a full rise on your toes. Take the calves through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Rise as high onto your toes as possible at the top.
Rise all the way onto your toes and squeeze your calves at the top.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
Lower under control into a full stretch at the bottom.
Pause briefly at the top to remove any bounce.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a two-count pause in the stretched position for extra range.
beginnerNotes: Do the movement on flat ground before adding a deficit or load.
equipmentSetup: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
difficultyConsiderations: The Calf Raise is an isolation machine movement. Because the machine guides the path, put your attention on driving with the target muscle. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because the machine guides the path, so there is little balance to manage, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Cable Calf Raise once you can control this one for all your reps.

whyItMatters: The Hamstring Stretch builds strength and size in your hamstrings. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Ease into the starting position without forcing the range.
Set a comfortable position you can control before moving.
executionSteps: Move to the first point of tension, not into pain.
Ease slightly deeper on each exhale.
Hold the end position briefly, then return smoothly to the start.
coachingTips: Move to the first point of tension rather than into pain.
Breathe out as you ease a little deeper into the range.
Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.
Feel the back of your thighs work through the rep.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
commonMistakes: Forcing or bouncing into an end range.
Holding your breath while you hold the position.
Snapping quickly from one rep to the next.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Forcing or bouncing into an end range.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Forcing past your range fights the stretch instead of easing it and does little for mobility.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly to gentle tension and let it ease with your breath.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Holding your breath while you hold the position.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Holding your breath tenses you up and stops you easing deeper into the range.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep breathing slowly and let each exhale ease you a little deeper.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Snapping quickly from one rep to the next.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Snapping through reps skips the controlled range that mobility work depends on.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly into and out of each repetition.

breathingGuidance: Breathe slowly and use each exhale to relax a little deeper.
tempoGuidance: Move slowly and hold positions rather than bouncing.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Work to a comfortable end range that eases over the set. Take the hamstrings through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Move to the first point of tension rather than into pain.
Feel the back of your thighs work through the rep.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Breathe out as you ease a little deeper into the range.
Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a gentle contraction at end range before relaxing deeper.
beginnerNotes: Reduce the range and build gradually session to session.
difficultyConsiderations: The Hamstring Stretch is a bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.

whyItMatters: The Leg Curl builds strength and size in your hamstrings. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set the pad or ankle strap just above your heels with your legs straight.
Take up the slack and start with your knees straight and the resistance under control.
executionSteps: Curl your heels toward your glutes by bending your knees.
Squeeze your hamstrings hard at the top of the curl.
Lower under control until your legs are straight.
coachingTips: Curl by bending at the knees while keeping your hips still.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top for a beat.
Lower all the way until your knees are straight each rep.
Feel the back of your thighs work through the rep.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips rise or the pelvis tilt to gain more range.
Cutting the curl short of a full hamstring squeeze.
Lowering too quickly on the way down.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the hips rise or the pelvis tilt to gain more range.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Extra range from the hips means your hamstrings do less of the curl.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hips pinned down and move only at the knees.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the curl short of a full hamstring squeeze.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Stopping short leaves the strongest part of the contraction untrained.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Curl your heels as close to your glutes as your range allows.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Lowering too quickly on the way down.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rushing the lower skips the part of the rep that builds the most control and strength.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower under control until your knees are straight.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

Lower all the way until your knees are straight each rep.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Cable Standing Leg Curl once you can control this one for all your reps.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Open at a pace you could hold to the end, then build.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Tension up top wastes energy that should go into your legs and lungs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Relax your hands, shoulders and face so the effort stays in your legs and lungs.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the effort drift down whenever your attention wanders.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Coasting drops the training effect for that stretch of the effort.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Check your pace regularly and hold it steady to the end.

Set a comfortable position you can control before moving.

Ease slightly deeper on each exhale.
Hold the end position briefly, then return smoothly to the start.

Breathe out as you ease a little deeper into the range.
Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.

Holding your breath while you hold the position.
Snapping quickly from one rep to the next.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Forcing past your range fights the stretch instead of easing it and does little for mobility.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly to gentle tension and let it ease with your breath.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Snapping through reps skips the controlled range that mobility work depends on.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Move slowly into and out of each repetition.

Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.

difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight.

Set a tall chest and brace before you descend.

Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
Complete all your reps on one side, then repeat with the other, matching the reps on your weaker side.

Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up as you descend and stand.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.

Cutting the depth short above parallel.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Knees caving in is a weaker position and takes force off your glutes.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes you lose your base and shift the squat onto your knees.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot planted and your weight over the mid-foot.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.

Keep your chest up as you descend and stand.

whyItMatters: The Side Plank builds strength and size in your rectus abdominis, hip flexors and obliques. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
setupInstructions: Set your position and take the slack out of your midsection before you begin.
Start each rep from a controlled, stable position.

Pause briefly where your midsection is working hardest.
Control the return rather than dropping quickly at the end.
coachingTips: Move under control — no yanking or rushing the reps.
Curl your ribs toward your hips rather than pulling with your neck.
Keep the tension on your midsection, not your hip flexors or lower back.
Curl your ribs toward your hips and feel your abs shorten.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.

Rushing through reps with momentum.
Arching the lower back away from a braced position.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Pulling your head does the work your abs should, so your midsection gets less out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hands light and lead the movement from your midsection.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing through reps with momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Momentum does the work your abs should, so the set does less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow each rep down and control both directions.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A loose lower back leaks force and takes the work off your abs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your ribs down and your midsection tight through the whole rep.

Set your grip evenly and pull your shoulder blades down and together.
Set your feet and create full-body tension before you begin.

Keep your forearms vertical as you lower.
Press back to a full lockout.
Complete all your reps on one side, then repeat with the other, matching the reps on your weaker side.

Tuck your elbows to about 45 degrees from your torso.
Drive your shoulder blades back and down and hold that position.

Match your effort to the band — its resistance climbs toward the end of the range.

Bouncing the load off the chest.
Losing the shoulder-blade set at the bottom.
Letting the band snap you back through the last part of the range.

mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Flared elbows put your shoulders in a weaker, less comfortable pressing position.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Point your elbows toward your hips as you lower.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Bouncing the load off the chest.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Bouncing skips the hardest part of the press, so you build less pressing strength.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the descent and pause briefly before you press.

Lower under control back to shoulder height.

whyItMatters: The Calf Raise builds strength and size in your calves. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set the balls of your feet on a stable surface with your heels free to drop.
Find a light hold for balance if you need it.
executionSteps: Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a beat at the top.
Lower under control until you feel a full stretch through your calves.
coachingTips: Rise as high onto your toes as possible at the top.
Lower under control into a full stretch at the bottom.
Pause briefly at the top to remove any bounce.
Rise all the way onto your toes and squeeze your calves at the top.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Short bounces use the tendon’s spring instead of your calves, so they do less work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Pause at the top and control a full stretch at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the stretch removes the part of the range that builds the most.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Let your heels drop below the platform for a full stretch.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rolling out sends force through the outside of your foot instead of your calves.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Drive evenly through your big toe and keep your ankles stacked.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A slammed stack means gravity did the lowering, not your muscles.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Control the return so the plates settle without banging.

tempoGuidance: Rise with control, pause at the top, then lower slowly.
rangeOfMotionNotes: Move from a deep heel-dropped stretch to a full rise on your toes. Take the calves through its full working range each rep.
cueHierarchy: Rise as high onto your toes as possible at the top.
Rise all the way onto your toes and squeeze your calves at the top.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
Lower under control into a full stretch at the bottom.
Pause briefly at the top to remove any bounce.
advancedCoachingNotes: Add a two-count pause in the stretched position for extra range.
beginnerNotes: Do the movement on flat ground before adding a deficit or load.
equipmentSetup: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
difficultyConsiderations: The Calf Raise is an isolation machine movement. Because the machine guides the path, put your attention on driving with the target muscle. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.
difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because the machine guides the path, so there is little balance to manage, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Cable Calf Raise once you can control this one for all your reps.

Set a comfortable position you can control before moving.

Move smoothly and slowly rather than bouncing.

setupInstructions: Adjust the seat and any pads so the working joint lines up with the machine’s pivot, set the pin to your working weight, and keep contact with the support pad throughout.
Set the pad or ankle strap just above your heels with your legs straight.
Take up the slack and start with your knees straight and the resistance under control.
executionSteps: Curl your heels toward your glutes by bending your knees.
Squeeze your hamstrings hard at the top of the curl.
Lower under control until your legs are straight.
coachingTips: Curl by bending at the knees while keeping your hips still.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top for a beat.
Lower all the way until your knees are straight each rep.
Feel the back of your thighs work through the rep.
Follow the machine’s guided lever path smoothly and control the weight back to the stack.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips rise or the pelvis tilt to gain more range.
Cutting the curl short of a full hamstring squeeze.
Lowering too quickly on the way down.
Letting the weight stack slam down at the bottom.
